item.title: Idempotent Producers: Eliminating Duplicate Messages
item.description: The Duplicate Problem With acks=all and retries enabled, a produce request might be acknowledged by the broker, but the acknowledgment is lost in the network before reaching the producer. The producer, seeing no response, retries — sending the same record again. The broker writes it a second time. item.title: Kafka Transactions and Exactly-Once Semantics
item.description: Why Transactions? At-least-once delivery means a record can be processed and produced more than once after a crash. For most applications, idempotent consumers handle this. But when you need a hard guarantee — either the produce happens and the offset commits, or neither does — you need Kafka transactions.
